purpose: Filter a dataset without losing the applied query or draft.
invariants: Immediate mode has no Apply action.
Explicit mode requires Apply and separates draft from applied filters.
Theme changes preserve draft and applied values.
This experiment supports customer query (text) and status (select: all, Active, Trial, Paused); other datasets require a new reviewed pattern contract.

host: records and optional explanatory source content
remote queries, persistence and broader dataset semantics

requirements.statement: Validate the supplied CompositionSpec and render an alert instead of controls/results when invalid. Supported controls are query text and status select with options drawn from all, Active, Trial and Paused; one or two controls are required.

In immediate mode filter from the current local draft and show no Apply action. In explicit mode keep local draft and applied values separate; Apply copies current pending values into applied state and the result status indicates unapplied changes.
Filter records by locale-lowercased substring across name, domain and owner together, and by exact selected status unless all. Do not trim, sort, fetch or mutate the provided record array.

Use all as the default status if declared, otherwise the first declared option. Reconcile an unavailable stored status to that default; omitted query/status controls stop contributing their respective filter.
Reset and empty-state Clear filters clear query and reset both local draft and applied status to the current default. Empty results retain table structure and add the configured empty message.
Keep draft/applied filters in the mounted renderer while applying declared mode/presentation attributes and table density. Changing those visual props does not intentionally reset React filter state.
Name the section from its heading, announce result count/unapplied state through a status region, and place the native table with scoped column headers in a named focusable scroll region.

Use validateCompositionSpec/resolveComposition for strict known properties, compatible Apply settings and registry/profile revision/hash checks. The renderer validates the spec shape/revision but does not compile a profile or verify a supplied active profile itself.

Provide stable unique record IDs and the declared customer fields/statuses. Records are host-owned; draft/applied filters are local to this mounted renderer and are not exported as a controlled filtering API.

Treat this as the finite customer-directory experiment. Other datasets, controls, remote filtering, loading/error state or persistence need an appropriate reviewed pattern contract, rather than assuming FilterBar behavior applies.
Use filtering group tokens for this composed pattern and preserve nested TextInput, Select, Button and Tag ownership. Keep dimensions independent from light/dark mode.

limitations: This renderer has no controlled draft/applied-state props, pagination, sorting, server filtering or asynchronous data lifecycle.
Unmounting resets local filters. Changing control availability can reveal or hide retained values; route or record-identity reset policy belongs to the host.
Deterministic recipe validation and source-backed requirements do not certify rendered accessibility or arbitrary customer data.
